claims.text: What the image looks like Buzzword: triple bubble on newborn AXR → jejunal atresia
Ex radiograph (prox jejunal atresia): lrg dilated loops in the upper abd w ⍉dist gas
claims.quote: This radiograph of an infant with proximal jejunal atresia shows large dilated loops in the upper abdomen with no distal gas.

claims.text: Aspects (abnorm in red) Postnatal plain abd radiograph may reveal dilated loops of sm bowel w air-fluid levels and a paucity of air in the colon and rectum; a barium enema reveals a microcolon (← disuse)
claims.quote: Postnatally, a plain abdominal radiograph is performed; it may reveal dilated loops of small bowel with air-fluid levels and a paucity of air in the colon and rectum. A barium enema reveals a microcolon (due to disuse).

claims.text: Prenatally, US showing dilated loops of sm bowel and polyhydramnios, or fetal MRI, may suggest or confirm the dx
claims.quote: Prenatally, ultrasound showing dilated loops of small bowel and polyhydramnios, or fetal MRI may suggest or confirm the diagnosis.

claims.text: Peritoneal calcifications suggest meconium peritonitis (a sign of intrauterine intestinal perf that can be seen in ≈ 10% of cases), which should raise sus of meconium ileus and CF
claims.quote: Peritoneal calcifications suggest the presence of meconium peritonitis, which is a sign of intrauterine intestinal perforation and can be seen in approximately 10% of cases. The presence of meconium peritonitis should raise suspicion of meconium ileus and cystic fibrosis (5).

claims.text: Types: I, a membrane completely occluding the lumen w the intestine intact; II, a gap w a fibrous cord b/n the segments; IIIA, a mesenteric gap w.o any connection; IIIB, jejunal atresia w ⍉dist SMA, the dist sm bowel coiled like an apple peel and a short gut; IV, multi atretic segments (string of sausages)
claims.quote: There are 5 major types of jejunoileal atresia (1): Type I consists of a membrane completely occluding the lumen with the intestine intact. Type II is a gap in the intestine with a fibrous cord between the proximal and distal segments of intestine. Type IIIA is a mesenteric gap without any connection between the segments. Type IIIB is jejunal atresia with absence of the distal superior mesenteric artery; the distal small bowel is coiled like an apple peel, and the gut is short. Type IV consists of multiple atretic segments (resembling a string of sausages).

claims.text: Eti An ischemic insult during preg: intussusception, perf, volvulus, intestinal strangulation via a hernia, or thromboembolism; maternal smoke and cocaine use have been assoc w intestinal atresia
claims.quote: Jejunoileal atresias occur as a result of an ischemic insult during pregnancy. The ischemic insult can be due to intussusception, perforation, volvulus, intestinal strangulation via a hernia, or thromboembolism. Maternal smoking and cocaine use have been associated with intestinal atresia (1).

claims.text: ≈ 1 in 10,000 live births, equally distributed b/n jejunum and ileum; assoc anomalies in up to ½ (most commonly urogenital); MC assoc conditions: congenital Hdz, CF, malrotation, gastroschisis
claims.quote: The estimated incidence is approximately 1 in 10,000 live births. Jejunoileal atresias are equally distributed between the jejunum and ileum (2–5). Associated congenital anomalies are seen in up to half of cases (6). The most common are urogenital anomalies. The most common associated conditions are congenital heart disease, cystic fibrosis, malrotation, and gastroschisis.

claims.text: Sx USU present late during day 1 or on day 2 of life w increasing abd distention, failure to pass stools, emesis and feeding problems; a Hx of polyhydramnios = common
claims.quote: Neonates with jejunoileal atresia usually present late during day 1 or on day 2 of life with increasing abdominal distention, failure to pass stools, emesis, and feeding problems. A history of polyhydramnios is common.

claims.text: Tx and next step Pre-op: NGT, NPO, IVF
claims.quote: Preoperative management of jejunoileal atresia consists of placing a nasogastric tube, giving nothing by mouth, and providing IV fluids.

claims.text: Surg repair = definitive: inspect the entire intestine for multi atresias; resect the atretic portion, USU w a primary anastomosis
claims.quote: Surgical repair is the definitive therapy. During surgery, the entire intestine should be inspected for multiple areas of atresia. The atretic portion is resected, usually with a primary anastomosis.

claims.text: Test for CF: 7 to 10% also have it (nearly 100% if meconium ileus = also present); screening for assoc anomalies should also be considered
claims.quote: Because 7 to 10% of patients also have cystic fibrosis (nearly 100% if meconium ileus is also present), testing for cystic fibrosis should be performed (1, 2). Screening for associated anomalies should also be considered.

claims.text: Prognosis = very good (> 90% survival), based on the length of remaining sm bowel and the presence of the ileocecal valve; short bowel syndrome requires parenteral nutrition for extended periods
claims.quote: The prognosis for infants with jejunoileal atresia is very good with > 90% survival (3, 4). Prognosis is based on the length of remaining small bowel and the presence of the ileocecal valve. Infants who subsequently develop short bowel syndrome require parenteral nutrition (PN) for extended periods (5).
